title: How to optimize your transaction management workflow on Mac: a guide for TCs
metaTitle: Optimize Your Transaction Management Workflow on Mac: A Guide for TCs
description: Master your transaction management workflow on Mac with tips to handle contract-to-close tasks, email, and documentation more efficiently.
intro: A successful transaction management workflow on Mac depends on your ability to handle high volumes of documentation while keeping every party informed. You act as the bridge between agents, lenders, and title companies, which means your desk is constantly shifting between email, CRM tools, and digital signing platforms.
tldr: Real estate transaction coordinators spend a large portion of their day on repetitive administrative tasks.
Centralizing your documentation in cloud-based tools is essential for maintaining a clean workflow.
Using a voice assistant like Lazur helps you navigate your Mac faster without taking your hands off the keyboard.
Focus your time on high-level coordination rather than manual data entry or email sorting.

blocks.text: Managing your daily transaction management workflow

Your morning starts with triage. You open your email and your transaction management platform. You check for new contracts. You verify that all signatures are present. You check the dates. You set up the digital file. This is the foundation of your day. If you miss a detail here, it creates a delay later.

You likely use tools like Dotloop, SkySlope, or Paperless Pipeline. These platforms are where your checklists live. When you are inside these apps, you need to be quick. You do not want to hunt for menu items. If you use a Mac, learn the native shortcuts. Use ⌘ + Space to open Spotlight and jump to your apps. Use ⌘ + Tab to switch between your browser and your email client.
Reducing the time spent on manual email

The average worker spends 28 percent of their week in their inbox. As a transaction coordinator, your number is likely higher. You send status updates to agents. You request missing documents from clients. You coordinate with title companies. This is where you lose time.

To improve your transaction management workflow, you must standardize your replies. Create templates in Gmail or Outlook. Never type the same email twice. If you have a standard list of requirements for a closing, save it as a snippet. When you need to send it, use a keyboard shortcut to trigger the text. This prevents errors and saves minutes on every single email.
How to use Lazur for your transaction tasks

Lazur sits in your Mac notch. It is a voice assistant that sees your screen. You hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on your screen. If you are lost in a complex menu in a tool like SkySlope, ask Lazur where a specific setting is. It will circle the button and label it for you. This saves you from digging through support pages.

If you need to draft a quick update, hold the fn key to dictate. You can speak your status update and have it appear in your email client as clean, formatted text. You do not need to worry about typos or formatting issues. Lazur handles the structure for you. It stays on your Mac and does not store your audio or screenshots.
Structuring your contract to close checklist

A formal checklist is the only way to ensure nothing falls through the cracks. Your list should cover every phase of the deal. Start with the contract execution. Move to the inspection period. Track the contingency deadlines. Finally, prepare for the closing day. You should have a template for every deal type.

Keep this checklist in a digital format. Google Sheets or a dedicated task manager works best. When you finish a task, check it off immediately. Do not rely on your memory. If you are working on a Mac, keep your checklist in a side window. Use ⌃ + ⌥ + ← or → to split your screen. This keeps your checklist visible while you work in other apps.
What to do when you hit an obstacle

Real estate is full of unexpected problems. An inspection might reveal a major issue. A lender might delay the loan approval. A title search might show an old lien. When these things happen, your workflow will break. You need a plan for these moments.

First, document the issue in your file. Second, notify the relevant parties. Third, update your timeline. Do not try to solve the legal or financial side yourself. Your job is to coordinate. If you need to research a local regulation, use Lazur to help you find the right information. Ask it to summarize the relevant parts of a document or a web page.

blocks.text: Common mistakes in transaction coordination

The most common mistake is manual data entry. If you are typing the same address or name into multiple systems, you are wasting time. Look for integrations between your CRM and your transaction platform. If no integration exists, use a clipboard manager. It allows you to copy multiple items and paste them as needed.

Another mistake is working without a backup. If you rely on a single cloud platform, what happens if it goes down? Always save a copy of your key documents on your local Mac or a secure backup drive. Follow your brokerage rules regarding data privacy and client information. Never store sensitive data in an insecure location.
Working with third parties

You deal with inspectors, lenders, and title agents every day. They have their own systems and their own timelines. You need to be the one who keeps them on track. Send reminders for upcoming deadlines. Ask for status updates before they become urgent. If you are proactive, you reduce the number of last-minute fires you have to put out.

When you communicate, be clear and direct. Use the subject line to your advantage. Include the property address and the purpose of the email. This helps people find your message in their own busy inboxes. If you need to attach a document, ensure it is named correctly. Use a format like YYYY-MM-DD-PropertyAddress-DocumentType.
Staying organized on a Mac

Your Mac is a powerful tool. Use its features to your advantage. Use Tags in Finder to label your files by status. For example, use a red tag for files that need urgent attention. Use a green tag for files that are ready for closing. This gives you a visual cue of your workload at a glance.

Use the built-in Calendar app to track your deadlines. Sync it with your work email so you never miss an appointment. If you have a lot of meetings, use the Focus feature in macOS to silence notifications. This helps you stay in the zone when you are working on a complex contract.
Professional duties and data handling

As a real estate professional, you handle sensitive data. You must follow your employer's rules on client data and privacy. Do not use tools that do not comply with your brokerage's security policies. If you are unsure about a tool, ask your broker or compliance officer. Never upload sensitive client documents to public AI tools that train on your data.

Lazur is built with privacy in mind. It does not store your audio or screen data. It does not use your content to train models. This makes it a safe choice for your daily work. You can use it to help you navigate your apps and draft text without compromising your clients' information.

faq.question: How can I speed up my transaction management workflow?
faq.answer: Standardize your email templates, use keyboard shortcuts for your most frequent tasks, and centralize your documentation in a single cloud platform.

faq.question: Is Lazur safe for handling real estate documents?
faq.answer: Lazur is designed for privacy. It does not store your audio or screen data, and it does not use your content to train its models. Always follow your brokerage's specific data security policies.

faq.question: What should I do if I spend too much time on email?
faq.answer: Use templates for recurring messages, implement a strict schedule for checking your inbox, and use a voice assistant to dictate replies quickly.

faq.question: How do I manage deadlines effectively?
faq.answer: Use a digital checklist in a tool like Google Sheets and sync your deadlines with your calendar. Review your upcoming tasks every morning.
